references.text: The angel of God who went before the camp of Israel is mentioned here as a protector for the people during their exodus from Egypt.
The Lord confirms that his angel will go before Moses and lead the people to the promised land.
God promises to send an angel ahead of the people to drive out the Canaanites and bring them into the land.
A reference to the angel who led Israel out of Egypt, a parallel to the promise of protection and guidance.
The commander of the Lord's army reveals himself to Joshua as a fulfillment of the promise of divine leadership into the land.
Isaiah describes how the angel of God's presence saved and carried the people through all days in times past.
The prophecy concerning the sending of a messenger who will clear the way, linked to the theme of God's angel going ahead.
Stephen's speech mentions the angel who revealed himself to Moses in the wilderness and led the people.
Paul describes how the fathers were guided by the cloud and passed through the sea, with Christ as the spiritual rock that followed them.
Angels are described as ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation, a continuation of the theme of angels' protective role.
A theological parallel where the motif of a forerunner clearing the way is fulfilled in the New Testament, even though the role shifts from angel to prophet.
An allusion to the same theological motif of a forerunner ensuring that God's people can reach their destination.
Repetition of the same prophetic quote linking the angelic guidance of Moses' time to John the Baptist's preparatory ministry.
A direct thematic parallel where an angel is sent to guard and guide a journey to a specific goal.
A theological parallel where a human (Joseph) fills the role of 'sent ahead' in the same way as the angel in Exodus.
